correctness.summary: For k>=1, the tree excess identity bounds the number of vertices above the degree window 1..k+1, and an explicit Prüfer-realizable degree sequence with at most one intermediate degree attains the bound. For k=0, the leaf identity gives n<=3R-2 and explicit {1,2,3}-degree profiles attain equality in every residue class. Exhaustive degree-multiset verification through order 40 found no discrepancy.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Caro--West (2009) gives the repetition lower bound and asymptotic tree sharpness; Caro--Lauri--Zarb (2019) gives the k>=1 tree spread lower bound and a sharpness construction whose displayed two-degree counts require a congruence condition; Caro--Skrekovski--Zarb (2026) does not state an all-order tree formula. Searches under exact and synonymous formulations found no prior statement of the fixed-order minima for every n. The lower bounds themselves are not claimed as new.

value.summary: The theorem closes the fixed-order residue gap for a standard sparse graph class, giving exact formulas for every order and every degree-window width, with explicit residue-correcting extremal degree sequences.

limitations: The theorem determines extremal values over trees but does not classify all extremal trees.
The lower-bound ingredients are prior work; the new claim is all-order exact attainment and fixed-order sharpness.
Differently phrased older degree-sequence literature and very recent unindexed work remain residual originality risks.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the symbolic proof.
